question: Does warning from deviations from a personal H/N/E conditional trajectory outperform warning from context-only residuals?
group_normalization: own-history, other-state history, and context predictor values and observation masks each divided by sqrt(group width)
reference_residuals: four held14-day blocks; training excludes held targets plus a seven-day buffer on each side; monitoring predictor fits all first56 days
control: own-history-reference changes the residual predictor only; raw H/N and context descriptors remain present and it is not a full network/environment ablation
shared: same296 coordinates, raw H/N, three8/16/32-day windows, risk head, original outcome and original participant folds
effect_coordinates: context coefficient L2 normalized by sqrt(supported context value count), and supported target fraction, same role as original context predictor
selection: validation AUROC, ties smaller C; both fixed variants reported on held development fold
external_test_use: none; already exposed external tests do not select this model
motivation: FCM forecasts normal temporal structure, but does not use a personal environmental reference
VAR EWS models dynamics directly, while short personal references require regularization
Original HNE context-only reference does not model own and cross-variable lag dynamics jointly
novelty_scope: regularized VARX and predictive residuals have prior art; this experiment examines their role in a shared sustained-disturbance warning framework
